name: ZE08-CH2O formaldehyde sensor
description: Winsen electrochemical formaldehyde (CH2O) detection module, 0-5 ppm (0-5000 ppb), resolution 0.01 ppm, with temperature compensation. Sends the concentration in ppb once a second over a 9600-baud UART (3 V logic) by default, and also has a 0.4-2 V DAC output and a PWM output. Runs on 3.7-9 V. Sold as: Winsen ZE08-CH2O module with its 7-pin 1.25 mm cable (pins 1-7: HD, DAC, GND, VIN, RXD, TXD, PWM).
eli5: Smells the air for formaldehyde, a gas that leaks out of new furniture, glue and paint, and tells your board how much there is.

pins.name: HD
pins.description: Pin 1: zero calibration, factory use only. Leave unconnected

pins.name: DAC
pins.description: Pin 2: analog output 0.4-2 V for 0-5 ppm (optional)

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Pin 4: supply 3.7-9 V (5 V is easiest), reverse-polarity protected

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: Pin 5: module serial input, 0-3.3 V: wire to the board's UART TX; only needed to send commands

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: Pin 6: module serial output, 0-3.3 V, 9600 baud: wire to the board's UART RX

pins.name: PWM
pins.description: Pin 7: PWM output proportional to concentration (optional)

supplierQuery: Winsen ZE08-CH2O formaldehyde sensor module UART
buildNotes: The module has a 7-pin 1.25 mm connector, not breadboard pins: use its cable and jumper wires.
Power VIN from 5 V (3.7-9 V allowed). The UART pins are 0-3.3 V, so TXD goes straight into an ESP32 or Pico RX pin.
Cross the serial wires: module TXD -> board RX, module RXD -> board TX (RXD is only needed to switch modes).

9600 baud 8N1. By default the module sends FF 17 04 00 CH CL 13 88 SUM once a second: concentration = CH*256 + CL in ppb, full range 0x1388 = 5000 ppb. SUM = (NOT(byte1+...+byte7)) + 1; drop frames that fail it.
Leave HD unconnected: pulling it low zero-calibrates the sensor and is for factory use only.
Let it warm up at least 3 minutes (5 minutes the first time) before trusting readings; keep it out of strong drafts and away from solvents and alcohol, which also read as formaldehyde.

driver.code:
# Winsen ZE08-CH2O electrochemical formaldehyde module, MicroPython driver.
# From the Winsen ZE08-CH2O user's manual V1.0: UART 9600 8N1, 3 V logic.
# Default mode is active upload: once a second the module sends a 9-byte frame
#   FF 17 04 00 CH CL RH RL SUM
#   0x17 = gas CH2O, 0x04 = unit ppb, 0x00 = no decimals,
#   concentration = CH*256 + CL (ppb), full range = RH*256 + RL (5000 ppb).
# SUM = (NOT (byte1 + ... + byte7)) + 1, 8 bits.
# Q&A mode (optional): send FF 01 86 00 00 00 00 00 79, reply
#   FF 86 UGH UGL 00 00 PPBH PPBL SUM (ug/m3 and ppb).
import time

CMD_QA_MODE = b'\xff\x01\x78\x41\x00\x00\x00\x00\x46'
CMD_ACTIVE_MODE = b'\xff\x01\x78\x40\x00\x00\x00\x00\x47'
CMD_READ = b'\xff\x01\x86\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x79'


def checksum(frame):
    return (~sum(frame[1:8]) + 1) & 0xFF


class ZE08:
    def __init__(self, uart):
        self.uart = uart
        self.full_range = None

    def _frame(self, head, timeout_ms):
        """Wait for a valid 9-byte frame whose bytes 0-1 are FF, head."""
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        buf = b''
        while time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) < timeout_ms:
            n = self.uart.any()
            if n:
                buf += self.uart.read(n)
                while len(buf) >= 9:
                    if buf[0] == 0xFF and buf[1] == head and checksum(buf) == buf[8]:
                        f = buf[:9]
                        return f
                    buf = buf[1:]
            else:
                time.sleep_ms(10)
        raise OSError('ZE08-CH2O: no valid frame (check TXD wiring, 9600 baud)')

    def read_ppb(self, timeout_ms=2500):
        """Active-upload mode (default): next concentration in ppb."""
        f = self._frame(0x17, timeout_ms)
        dec = f[3]
        self.full_range = (f[6] << 8) | f[7]
        v = (f[4] << 8) | f[5]
        return v / (10 ** dec) if dec else v

    def read_ppm(self, timeout_ms=2500):
        return self.read_ppb(timeout_ms) / 1000

    def set_qa_mode(self):
        self.uart.write(CMD_QA_MODE)

    def set_active_mode(self):
        self.uart.write(CMD_ACTIVE_MODE)

    def query(self, timeout_ms=1000):
        """Q&A mode only: returns (ug/m3, ppb)."""
        while self.uart.any():
            self.uart.read()
        self.uart.write(CMD_READ)
        f = self._frame(0x86, timeout_ms)
        return (f[2] << 8) | f[3], (f[6] << 8) | f[7]

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
from ze08 import ZE08

uart = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, tx=Pin({RXD}), rx=Pin({TXD}))
sensor = ZE08(uart)
while True:
    ppb = sensor.read_ppb()
    print('CH2O=%d ppb (%.3f ppm)' % (ppb, ppb / 1000))
